newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS, ELEKTA ANNOUNCE RADIATION THERAPY MERGER.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS, ELEKTA ANNOUNCE RADIATION THERAPY MERGER.

text.p: Electronics giant Philips said on Thursday its Medical Systems division would merge its radiation therapy activities with those of Swedish Elekta AB.
Under the deal, Philips will take a substantial minority stake in Elekta, a leading supplier of advanced neuroscience equipment and precision cancer treatment, Philips said.

"Philips Medical Systems...and Elekta...are announcing plans to merge Philips' global radiation therapy activities with Elekta's activities and bring them under common control of Elekta," the statement said.

A new organization is planned in which "...Philips' sales and service organizations will handle the interface with customers while Elekta is to assume overall ownership of the radiotherapy business," the statement said.
The new organization is to provide the medical community with products, information and support services dedicated specifically to the radiation therapy field.
